Document type/version: Project schedule and contract documents

1. INTRODUCTION

This document forms Part 1 of the project schedule and contract documentation for the Meridian Crossrail Interchange (hereafter "the Interchange project" or "MCI"). It records the baseline programme, key contractual dates, and early milestone definitions agreed between the Employer, the Main Contractor (Meridian Construction JV), and the Project Controls Office.

The schedule information contained herein is governed by the Project Controls Procedures (PCP-MCI-002, Rev 3). All dates are expressed in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). All times are given in Europe/London timezone unless otherwise stated. Business days exclude weekends and all UK public holidays, as defined in the Contract Particulars, Schedule 5.

This Part 1 document covers the period from project inception through to the end of the mobilisation phase and the first reporting cycle. It is intended to be read in conjunction with the monthly schedule updates (MCI-PCO-SCH-0xx series) and the exception log (MCI-PCO-EXL-001 series).

2. PROJECT OVERVIEW

The Meridian Crossrail Interchange is a major transport infrastructure project located in the West Midlands, comprising:

- A new four-platform underground station box (platforms 1–4)
- North and south concourses with retail and passenger facilities
- Track and signalling interface works to the existing Crossrail mainline
- A bus interchange and cycle hub on the north side
- Landscaping and public realm works

The project is being delivered under a Design and Build contract with a target completion date of 2026-03-31. The contract includes provisions for extension of time (EOT) in accordance with Clause 43 of the Conditions of Contract.

3. SCHEDULED START DATE

The project schedule records that the Meridian Crossrail Interchange scheduled_start_date is 2024-01-08. Record status: current.

This date represents the contractual commencement of the works and the start of the mobilisation period. It was agreed at the pre-contract meeting held on 2023-12-19 and ratified in the Letter of Acceptance issued on 2024-01-03.

The scheduled start date is a current controlled entry within the project schedule. No revisions or amendments have been made to this date as of the issue of this Part 1 document. Any proposed change to this date would require a formal EOT application and approval through the Project Controls Office.

4. BASELINE PROGRAMME SUMMARY

The baseline programme (MCI-PCO-SCH-001-BL, Rev 0) was issued on 2024-01-05 and covers the period from 2024-01-08 to 2026-03-31. The programme is structured around the following key work packages:

| Work Package | Package ID | Planned Start | Planned Finish | Duration (weeks) |
|--------------|------------|---------------|----------------|------------------|
| Mobilisation and site establishment | MCI-WP-001 | 2024-01-08 | 2024-02-23 | 7 |
| Enabling works and demolition | MCI-WP-002 | 2024-02-26 | 2024-05-31 | 14 |
| Diaphragm walling (north box) | MCI-WP-003 | 2024-06-03 | 2024-09-27 | 17 |
| Diaphragm walling (south box) | MCI-WP-004 | 2024-07-01 | 2024-10-25 | 17 |
| Bulk excavation | MCI-WP-005 | 2024-10-28 | 2025-02-28 | 18 |
| Structural works – base slab | MCI-WP-006 | 2025-03-03 | 2025-06-27 | 17 |
| Structural works – platform level | MCI-WP-007 | 2025-06-30 | 2025-10-31 | 18 |
| Fit-out and M&E works | MCI-WP-008 | 2025-11-03 | 2026-02-27 | 17 |
| Testing and commissioning | MCI-WP-009 | 2026-03-02 | 2026-03-27 | 4 |

Note: The above durations are measured in working weeks (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays). Float within each work package is not shown in this summary; refer to the full baseline programme for detailed float and critical path analysis.

5. EARLY MILESTONES

The following milestones are defined for the initial phase of the project. These are contractual milestones and are subject to the provisions of the Contract Particulars, Schedule 6.

| Milestone ID | Description | Target Date | Reporting Frequency |
|--------------|-------------|-------------|---------------------|
| M-001 | Commencement of works (mobilisation) | 2024-01-08 | One-off |

| M-003 | Site compound fully operational | 2024-02-02 | Weekly |

| M-005 | Demolition of existing structures complete | 2024-05-31 | Monthly |
| M-006 | Diaphragm walling plant mobilised | 2024-06-03 | Monthly |
| M-007 | North box diaphragm walling complete | 2024-09-27 | Monthly |

The following table sets out the key contractual milestones for the completion phase of the works. These milestones are defined in the Contract Particulars, Schedule 6, and are subject to the provisions of the contract for delay and EOT.

Note: The target dates for M-009 through M-013 are programme dates for planning purposes. The contractual date for completion of the whole of the works is the scheduled finish date of 2024-12-20. Any change to the scheduled finish date requires a formal EOT application and approval in accordance with the contract.

**8. SCHEDULE UPDATE AND REPORTING PROTOCOL**

The Project Controls Office operates a monthly schedule update cycle. The following protocol applies to all schedule submissions and updates:

- **Baseline programme**: The accepted baseline programme is the reference against which progress is measured. The baseline programme is identified as Revision 1.0 and is dated 2024-01-05.
- **Monthly updates**: Each monthly update shall be issued within five business days of the end of the reporting period. Updates shall reflect actual progress, approved changes, and any approved EOTs.
- **Schedule health**: Each update shall include a schedule health check, covering critical path analysis, float consumption, and the status of all contractual milestones.
- **Change control**: Any change to the scheduled finish date of 2024-12-20 shall only be made following a formal EOT application and approval by the Project Manager. No unauthorised changes to the scheduled finish date are permitted.
- **Reporting calendar**: Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays. All reporting dates are based on the Europe/London timezone.

The following table summarises the schedule update cycle for the remainder of the project:

| Reporting Period | Update Issue Date | Reporting Period | Update Issue Date |
|------------------|-------------------|------------------|-------------------|
| January 2024 | 2024-02-07 | July 2024 | 2024-08-07 |
| February 2024 | 2024-03-06 | August 2024 | 2024-09-04 |
| March 2024 | 2024-04-03 | September 2024 | 2024-10-02 |
| April 2024 | 2024-05-01 | October 2024 | 2024-10-30 |
| May 2024 | 2024-06-05 | November 2024 | 2024-12-04 |
| June 2024 | 2024-07-03 | December 2024 | 2025-01-08 |

According to the schedule, the Meridian Crossrail Interchange scheduled_finish_date is 2024-12-20. Record status: current.

**9. EXTENSION OF TIME (EOT) PROVISIONS**

The contract provides for EOT in the event of delay caused by a listed event. The following provisions apply:

- **Application**: The contractor shall submit an EOT application within 14 days of becoming aware of the delay event.
- **Assessment**: The Project Manager shall assess the application within 28 days of receipt, considering the impact on the scheduled finish date of 2024-12-20.
- **Record**: All EOT applications and assessments shall be recorded in the project change log and shall be reflected in the monthly schedule update.
- **Status**: EOT applications that are approved shall be reflected as a revision to the scheduled finish date. EOT applications that are not approved shall be recorded as such, and the scheduled finish date shall remain unchanged.

As of the date of this document, no EOT applications have been approved. The scheduled finish date of 2024-12-20 remains current.

**10. CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS AND NOTICES**

The following contractual obligations are noted for the attention of all parties:
**10.3 Notices and Communications**

- All formal notices, including those relating to delays, variations, or claims, shall be in writing and shall be delivered to the registered office of the receiving party or to the address specified in the Contract Agreement. Notices sent by email shall be deemed received on the next business day following transmission, provided that a read receipt is requested and obtained.
- The Contractor shall notify the Project Manager in writing within 5 business days of any event that may affect the scheduled finish date, the quality of the Works, or the safety of personnel or the public. This notification shall be without prejudice to any subsequent EOT application.
- For the avoidance of doubt, the use of the project collaboration platform (Meridian Portal) for routine correspondence does not constitute formal notice under the Contract. Formal notices must be issued in accordance with this Clause 10.3.

**10.4 Variations**

- No variation to the Works shall be instructed or carried out without a written instruction from the Project Manager. Verbal instructions shall be confirmed in writing by the Contractor within 7 days, and if not confirmed or rejected by the Project Manager within a further 7 days, shall be deemed to be a written instruction.
- Each variation instruction shall be assessed for its impact on time and cost. The Contractor shall provide a quotation for any variation within 14 days of receipt of the instruction, unless the Project Manager directs otherwise.
- Variations that affect the critical path may result in an adjustment to the scheduled finish date. Such adjustments shall be made only through the EOT procedure set out in Section 9, and not through the variation instruction itself.

**10.5 Quality and Non-Conformance**

- The Contractor shall maintain a quality management system in accordance with ISO 9001:2015 and the project quality plan. The quality plan shall be submitted to the Project Manager for approval within 28 days of the Contract Start Date.
- Any work that does not conform to the Contract requirements shall be identified by a Non-Conformance Report (NCR). The Contractor shall open an NCR for each instance of non-conformance and shall propose a disposition within 7 days. The disposition shall be either: rectification, acceptance without rectification, or rejection.
- The Contractor shall maintain a register of all NCRs and shall include a summary of open and closed NCRs in each monthly progress report. The Project Manager shall have the right to inspect the NCR register at any time.

**10.6 Health, Safety, and Environment**

- The Contractor shall comply with the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 and shall appoint a Principal Designer and a Principal Contractor as required by those Regulations. The Contractor shall provide evidence of these appointments to the Project Manager within 14 days of the Contract Start Date.
- The Contractor shall prepare and maintain a Construction Phase Plan in accordance with CDM 2015. The plan shall be reviewed and updated at intervals not exceeding 3 months, or more frequently if there is a significant change to the Works or the site conditions.
- The Contractor shall report all reportable incidents under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013 (RIDDOR) to the Project Manager within 24 hours of the incident, and shall provide a written report within 7 days.

**10.7 Insurance and Indemnities**

- The Contractor shall maintain, at its own cost, the insurances required by the Contract Agreement, including employer's liability insurance, public liability insurance, and contractor's all-risk insurance. Evidence of such insurances shall be provided to the Project Manager prior to the Contract Start Date and thereafter upon renewal.
- The Contractor shall indemnify the Employer against all claims, costs, and expenses arising out of any negligence or breach of contract by the Contractor, its subcontractors, or its agents.
**11. Schedule Management and Reporting**

**11.1 General**

The Contractor shall prepare and maintain a detailed construction programme in accordance with the requirements of the Contract. The programme shall be developed using the planning software specified in the Contract Particulars and shall be issued in both native and PDF formats. All programmes shall be submitted to the Project Manager for review and no works shall commence in any area prior to the acceptance of the programme covering that area.

The programme shall be prepared on a time-scaled basis and shall show, as a minimum:

- The commencement and completion dates of each activity
- The sequence of works and any constraints or dependencies
- The critical path, clearly identified
- The float available on non-critical activities
- The location of each activity, where applicable
- The resources assigned to each activity, including labour, plant, and materials
- The milestones identified in the Contract

**11.2 Baseline Programme**

Within 21 days of the Contract Start Date, the Contractor shall submit a baseline programme for the whole of the Works. The baseline programme shall be submitted in accordance with the requirements of Clause 11.1 and shall be accompanied by a written narrative describing the principal assumptions, constraints, and methodology used in its preparation.

The baseline programme shall be approved by the Project Manager prior to the commencement of any works. The Project Manager shall respond to the Contractor's submission within 10 business days of receipt. The Contractor shall incorporate any reasonable comments made by the Project Manager and shall resubmit the programme within 5 business days of receipt of such comments.

Once accepted, the baseline programme shall be the reference programme against which progress and any extensions of time shall be measured. No changes to the baseline programme shall be made without the prior written approval of the Project Manager in accordance with the change control procedures set out in Clause 13.

**11.3 Programme Updates**

The Contractor shall submit an updated programme to the Project Manager on a monthly basis, not later than the 5th business day of each calendar month. The updated programme shall reflect the actual progress of the Works as at the last day of the preceding month and shall be accompanied by:

- A progress report in the format set out in the Contract Particulars
- A narrative report describing the progress made, any delays encountered, and the measures proposed to recover any slippage
- A comparison of the updated programme against the baseline programme, identifying any variances
- A forecast of the works to be undertaken in the next 2 months

The updated programme shall be submitted in native format and shall not be watermarked or otherwise restricted. The Project Manager shall review the updated programme and shall either accept it or return it with comments within 10 business days of receipt. The Contractor shall amend the programme in accordance with any reasonable comments and shall resubmit it within 5 business days.

Where the updated programme shows that the Works will not be completed by the Date for Completion, the Contractor shall identify the reasons for the delay and shall include a recovery plan demonstrating how the Contractor intends to achieve completion. The recovery plan shall be submitted separately and shall be updated at each monthly reporting cycle until the delay is recovered or the programme is otherwise revised in accordance with the Contract.

**11.4 Progress Meetings**

Progress meetings shall be held at monthly intervals, or at such other frequency as the Project Manager may reasonably direct. The Contractor shall attend all progress meetings and shall be represented by a person with authority to make decisions on behalf of the Contractor.

The Contractor shall circulate the agenda for each progress meeting not less than 5 business days prior to the meeting. **General Procedure – Log Maintenance and Reporting**

This log is maintained by the Site Works Manager and is reviewed weekly at the project controls meeting. All entries are numbered sequentially and should be made within 24 hours of the event being identified, or as soon as practicable where access to the log is not available (e.g. during periods of leave or when working off site). The log is held in the site office and is also available in read-only format on the shared drive. Any member of the site team may request an entry, but only the Site Works Manager or their nominated deputy can raise or amend an entry.

Entries are not to be deleted. If an entry is raised in error, it shall be marked as "Void" and a new entry raised where necessary. Corrections to an entry shall be made by adding a note to the original entry; the original text shall not be overwritten. This is to maintain an accurate audit trail.

---

**Severity Definitions**

- **Critical** – An event that has caused, or has the potential to cause, a significant safety risk, structural damage, a stop to works, or a material impact on the programme that cannot be recovered within the float. Critical entries require immediate notification to the Project Manager and the client's representative. An NCR or incident report will normally be raised.
- **Major** – An event that has caused, or is likely to cause, a delay to a key activity, a cost impact, or a breach of a statutory or contractual requirement. Major entries shall be reported to the Project Manager within 24 hours. A formal notification may be required, depending on the nature of the event.
- **Minor** – An event that has been resolved without significant impact on the programme or cost, or where the impact is contained within the existing float. Minor entries are recorded for information and trend analysis.

---

**Reporting Requirements**

- **Critical** – Verbally notify the Project Manager immediately, followed by a written notification (email or formal letter) within 4 hours. An entry shall be made in this log on the same day.
- **Major** – Notify the Project Manager in writing (email is acceptable) within 24 hours. An entry shall be made in this log within 24 hours.
- **Minor** – Record in this log within 24 hours. No separate notification is required unless the event is part of a recurring trend.

It is the responsibility of the person identifying the event to ensure an entry is raised. If the Site Works Manager is not available, the entry may be raised by the deputy and countersigned by the Site Works Manager at the earliest opportunity.

1. INTRODUCTION

This document forms Part 1 of the project schedule and contract documentation for the Meridian Crossrail Interchange (hereafter "the Interchange project" or "MCI"). It records the baseline programme, key contractual dates, and early milestone definitions agreed between the Employer, the Main Contractor (Meridian Construction JV), and the Project Controls Office.

The schedule information contained herein is governed by the Project Controls Procedures (PCP-MCI-002, Rev 3). All dates are expressed in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). All times are given in Europe/London timezone unless otherwise stated. Business days exclude weekends and all UK public holidays, as defined in the Contract Particulars, Schedule 5.

This Part 1 document covers the period from project inception through to the end of the mobilisation phase and the first reporting cycle. It is intended to be read in conjunction with the monthly schedule updates (MCI-PCO-SCH-0xx series) and the exception log (MCI-PCO-EXL-001 series).

2. PROJECT OVERVIEW

The Meridian Crossrail Interchange is a major transport infrastructure project located in the West Midlands, comprising:

- A new four-platform underground station box (platforms 1–4)
- North and south concourses with retail and passenger facilities
- Track and signalling interface works to the existing Crossrail mainline
- A bus interchange and cycle hub on the north side
- Landscaping and public realm works

The project is being delivered under a Design and Build contract with a target completion date of 2026-03-31. The contract includes provisions for extension of time (EOT) in accordance with Clause 43 of the Conditions of Contract.

3. SCHEDULED START DATE

The project schedule records that the Meridian Crossrail Interchange scheduled_start_date is 2024-01-08. Record status: current.

This date represents the contractual commencement of the works and the start of the mobilisation period. It was agreed at the pre-contract meeting held on 2023-12-19 and ratified in the Letter of Acceptance issued on 2024-01-03.

The scheduled start date is a current controlled entry within the project schedule. No revisions or amendments have been made to this date as of the issue of this Part 1 document. Any proposed change to this date would require a formal EOT application and approval through the Project Controls Office.

4. BASELINE PROGRAMME SUMMARY

The baseline programme (MCI-PCO-SCH-001-BL, Rev 0) was issued on 2024-01-05 and covers the period from 2024-01-08 to 2026-03-31. The programme is structured around the following key work packages:

**11. Schedule Management and Reporting**

**11.1 General**

The Contractor shall prepare and maintain a detailed construction programme in accordance with the requirements of the Contract. The programme shall be developed using the planning software specified in the Contract Particulars and shall be issued in both native and PDF formats. All programmes shall be submitted to the Project Manager for review and no works shall commence in any area prior to the acceptance of the programme covering that area.

The programme shall be prepared on a time-scaled basis and shall show, as a minimum:

- The commencement and completion dates of each activity
- The sequence of works and any constraints or dependencies
- The critical path, clearly identified
- The float available on non-critical activities
- The location of each activity, where applicable
- The resources assigned to each activity, including labour, plant, and materials
- The milestones identified in the Contract

**11.2 Baseline Programme**

Within 21 days of the Contract Start Date, the Contractor shall submit a baseline programme for the whole of the Works. The baseline programme shall be submitted in accordance with the requirements of Clause 11.1 and shall be accompanied by a written narrative describing the principal assumptions, constraints, and methodology used in its preparation.

The baseline programme shall be approved by the Project Manager prior to the commencement of any works. The Project Manager shall respond to the Contractor's submission within 10 business days of receipt. The Contractor shall incorporate any reasonable comments made by the Project Manager and shall resubmit the programme within 5 business days of receipt of such comments.

Once accepted, the baseline programme shall be the reference programme against which progress and any extensions of time shall be measured. No changes to the baseline programme shall be made without the prior written approval of the Project Manager in accordance with the change control procedures set out in Clause 13.

**11.3 Programme Updates**

The Contractor shall submit an updated programme to the Project Manager on a monthly basis, not later than the 5th business day of each calendar month. The updated programme shall reflect the actual progress of the Works as at the last day of the preceding month and shall be accompanied by:

- A progress report in the format set out in the Contract Particulars
- A narrative report describing the progress made, any delays encountered, and the measures proposed to recover any slippage
- A comparison of the updated programme against the baseline programme, identifying any variances
- A forecast of the works to be undertaken in the next 2 months

The updated programme shall be submitted in native format and shall not be watermarked or otherwise restricted. The Project Manager shall review the updated programme and shall either accept it or return it with comments within 10 business days of receipt. The Contractor shall amend the programme in accordance with any reasonable comments and shall resubmit it within 5 business days.

Where the updated programme shows that the Works will not be completed by the Date for Completion, the Contractor shall identify the reasons for the delay and shall include a recovery plan demonstrating how the Contractor intends to achieve completion. The recovery plan shall be submitted separately and shall be updated at each monthly reporting cycle until the delay is recovered or the programme is otherwise revised in accordance with the Contract.

**11.4 Progress Meetings**

Progress meetings shall be held at monthly intervals, or at such other frequency as the Project Manager may reasonably direct. The Contractor shall attend all progress meetings and shall be represented by a person with authority to make decisions on behalf of the Contractor.

The Contractor shall circulate the agenda for each progress meeting not less than 5 business days prior to the meeting. **General Procedure – Log Maintenance and Reporting**

This log is maintained by the Site Works Manager and is reviewed weekly at the project controls meeting. All entries are numbered sequentially and should be made within 24 hours of the event being identified, or as soon as practicable where access to the log is not available (e.g. during periods of leave or when working off site). The log is held in the site office and is also available in read-only format on the shared drive. Any member of the site team may request an entry, but only the Site Works Manager or their nominated deputy can raise or amend an entry.

Entries are not to be deleted. If an entry is raised in error, it shall be marked as "Void" and a new entry raised where necessary. Corrections to an entry shall be made by adding a note to the original entry; the original text shall not be overwritten. This is to maintain an accurate audit trail.

---

**Severity Definitions**

- **Critical** – An event that has caused, or has the potential to cause, a significant safety risk, structural damage, a stop to works, or a material impact on the programme that cannot be recovered within the float. Critical entries require immediate notification to the Project Manager and the client's representative. An NCR or incident report will normally be raised.
- **Major** – An event that has caused, or is likely to cause, a delay to a key activity, a cost impact, or a breach of a statutory or contractual requirement. Major entries shall be reported to the Project Manager within 24 hours. A formal notification may be required, depending on the nature of the event.
- **Minor** – An event that has been resolved without significant impact on the programme or cost, or where the impact is contained within the existing float. Minor entries are recorded for information and trend analysis.

---

**Reporting Requirements**

- **Critical** – Verbally notify the Project Manager immediately, followed by a written notification (email or formal letter) within 4 hours. An entry shall be made in this log on the same day.
- **Major** – Notify the Project Manager in writing (email is acceptable) within 24 hours. An entry shall be made in this log within 24 hours.
- **Minor** – Record in this log within 24 hours. No separate notification is required unless the event is part of a recurring trend.

It is the responsibility of the person identifying the event to ensure an entry is raised. If the Site Works Manager is not available, the entry may be raised by the deputy and countersigned by the Site Works Manager at the earliest opportunity.
